final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no genuinely new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrowing is useful but not sufficient to move the claim to compliant_with_caveats on the present evidence. The admissible record still shows a 1.4-point gap in a named launch use case, an open legal ticket on whether disclosure is required, and no evidence of completed disclosure or approved pre-launch risk acceptance. Under the stated policy, those are unresolved compliance predicates. It is reasonable to distinguish overall release readiness from the stronger claim of policy-compliant certification for launch, but the audited claim remains insufficiently supported insofar as it relies on documentation and post-launch monitoring instead of proof that the named-use-case disclosure condition was satisfied or formally excepted.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the immigration-services intake limitation was disclosed before launch.
No new admissible evidence shows approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering the named launch use case.
Legal review remains open, so a policy predicate tied to materiality and disclosure is unresolved.
The affected segment is still admissibly shown to be a named launch use case in rollout commitments, which weighs toward materiality under the policy text.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the policy's specific disclosure condition for material limitations.
Public governance guidance on documentation and monitoring does not replace the repo policy requirement for disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance.
